title: GuidedBench: Measuring and Mitigating the Evaluation Discrepancies of In-the-wild LLM Jailbreak Methods
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: A benchmark pairs a guideline-based evaluation scheme with a curated dataset and a procedure for generating case-specific guidelines.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, labeled (a)-(c), colored set boxes at bottom of middle panel
description: Three-panel figure with captions (a), (b) and (c) along the bottom. Panel (a), Overview of GuidedEval, has a top row of three boxes: Evaluation Guidelines (dashed gray), Harmful Question (blue) and Jailbreak Response (orange). Below is a rounded card showing a guideline-based scoring checklist. Entity and action items are marked with green Detected or red Not Detected badges, and the card gives ASR = 3/4 = 75%. abstract: Despite the growing interest in jailbreaks as an effective red-teaming tool for building safe and responsible large language models (LLMs), flawed evaluation system designs have led to significant discrepancies in their effectiveness assessments. With a systematic measurement study based on 37 jailbreak studies since 2022, we find that existing evaluation systems lack case-specific criteria, resulting in misleading conclusions about their effectiveness and safety implications. In this paper, we introduce GuidedBench, a novel benchmark comprising a curated harmful question dataset and GuidedEval, an evaluation system integrated with detailed case-by-case evaluation guidelines. Experiments demonstrate that GuidedBench offers more accurate evaluations of jailbreak performance, enabling meaningful comparisons across methods. GuidedEval reduces inter-evaluator variance by at least 76.03%, ensuring reliable and reproducible evaluations. We reveal why existing jailbreak benchmarks fail to evaluate accurately and suggest better evaluation practices.
